text:
maya: Noticed some confusion in the last usability run: people don't know whether the short `k/M` next to the axis is interactive. Proposing two UX patterns to test: (1) persistent unit pill at top-right of chart that always shows full unit (e.g., "req/s") and can be tapped for copy/details; (2) inline abbrev on ticks with an explicit `abbr` tooltip on hover/focus. Which feels less noisy?

jamal: I like the unit pill for dense charts because it separates label from tick clutter. Tech note: the pill lets us avoid calc-heavy layout changes. We can render as absolutely positioned element inside the chart container. Need to make sure it doesn't overlap series legends.

lucy: UX: pill works for desktop but might be too small on mobile if we absolute-position; we can move it into the legend area on narrow widths. Also copy: call it "Unit" (singular) and include an optional short description beneath in the pill (gray, smaller). Example: "Unit: requests/sec" then "(avg over 1m)" in smaller text.

ava: Accessibility: ensure the pill is keyboard-focusable and uses aria-describedby to point to a hidden element that contains the full unit explanation. Avoid relying solely on hover tooltips. For the inline abbr approach, add `abbr` with `title` but also expose the full string via `aria-label` on the axis element.

kai: Smoothing debate: on these charts some folks prefer a light moving-average smoothing to reduce flicker in the mini charts. I propose we implement smoothing as a client-side resampler rather than altering the raw data so the underlying datapoints still show on hover. That gives the best of both worlds.

rafael: Outlier handling idea: instead of dim or inset, we could introduce a separate visual treatment: a thin dashed cap marker at the top with a tooltip showing the true value. Keeps the main y-scale unchanged and avoids distorting perception. Will add a sketch.

maya: That dashed-cap marker is interesting. How does it behave in streaming charts? If spikes are frequent the cap might swamp the axis.

rafael: For streaming, cap markers would auto-collapse into a single density indicator when more than N spikes in a 1m window. The density indicator shows count and allows expanding to list.

jamal: Implementation constraints: adding a density indicator + caps will increase per-frame draw work. For GPU-backed canvas we should be fine, but SVG with many series might be costly. Also we need to preserve hit-testing for hover.

lucy: Copy wording — avoid words like "suppress" or "hide". Use "de-emphasize" or "compact spikes". For the setting label we could try: "De-emphasize extreme spikes (visual only)" with a tooltip explaining we do not remove data.

ava: A11y extra: when a chart updates and a spike is de-emphasized or capped, announce a short text via ARIA live region like: "Large spike detected at 11:04 AM, value 12,300 requests per second." Make this optional in settings for noise-sensitive screen reader users.

kai: Quick CSS idea for pill mobility so it moves into legend on small screens:

```css
.chart__unit-pill {
  position: absolute;
  right: 12px;
  top: 8px;
}
@media (max-width: 480px) {
  .chart__unit-pill { position: static; margin-left: 8px; }
}
```

jamal: For axis abbrevs: avoid ambiguity. If ticks are 0.45k vs 450 we should prefer `450` not `0.45k`. Abbrev only at >=1000. Also ensure negative values keep sign near number, not in pill.

maya: Test plan: build a lightweight A/B using playground charts: variant A (unit pill + cap markers), variant B (inline abbr + dimmed spikes). Recruit 8 users: 4 data platform engineers, 2 PMs, 2 accessibility testers. Measure: time-to-identify-largest-spike and preference.

rafael: I'll add a Figma quick mock and a tiny GIF showing streaming with caps vs dimming: https://www.figma.com/file/FAKE/caps-vs-dim

design-bot: New mock uploaded by rafael: https://redwood-inference.design/mocks/caps-vs-dim-2026-03-23.png :frame_with_picture:
